acceptance: A fixture simulates the crash window: a PR is created, then the run crashes before the PR URL is recorded
The next run discovers the existing PR and adopts it instead of opening a duplicate
The fixture proves the PR-create operation was invoked exactly once across the crash and the recovery
The fixture touches no production repository: it uses a stubbed gh (no GitHub writes) or an isolated scratch repo, never garzonandres2004/genesis or any production repo
Work lands on branch phase2/crash-pr-recovery via PR; merge only by the orchestrator after verification
evidence: Builder commit 2dd8e41e0d2cc7d7efd23b48f4d4e747ac16b1a7 pushed to origin/phase2/crash-pr-recovery (remote SHA confirmed by orchestrator); 3 new files only, 186 insertions, pr-adopt.mjs unchanged (findExistingPr already exported)
Orchestrator re-ran npm test in worktree: 61 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (pre-existing root skip); 7 new tests pass

Crash-then-adopt verified in test code: run 1 pr-create (URL deliberately discarded, nothing written), run 2 adoptPr returns the exact URL + headSha with null anomaly and the record is written from it; assert pr-create count == 1 across both runs; empty-PATH guard + ENOENT test prove no real gh spawn
headRefOid field verified by orchestrator against real gh (read-only): PR #20 returns headRefOid 50ed64f, the branch's post-record head — closing the builder's unverified-field caveat

Not proven: no live GitHub crash reproduced (fixture proves the logic; live path only partly proven earlier via pr-adopt on a real branch); runner wiring deferred to the Phase 2 plan as follow-up; parallel execution stays OFF
objective: Prove crash-after-PR recovery in an isolated fixture: after a crash between PR creation and PR URL recording, the next run must adopt the existing PR, not create a duplicate.
title: Phase 2: Prove crash-after-PR recovery
